raw: | A Mendix 11.14 project will not build (`error: release version 25 not supported`) or, if built elsewhere, will not boot (`UnsupportedClassVersionError … class file version 69.0`) | mxcli resolved a JDK **21 unconditionally** and refused any other `JAVA_HOME`. Studio Pro 11.14 supports Java 25 and its blank app asks for it, so the Java release is now a per-project variable (Settings > Model > JavaVersion) rather than a constant | `cmd/mxcli/docker/javaversion.go` (`ProjectJavaMajor`, `ParseJavaMajor`), `cmd/mxcli/docker/detect.go` (`resolveJDK`, `isJDK`, `jdkSearchPathsFor`); the four call sites are `build.go`, `settle.go`, `mxserve.go`, `localboot.go` | **Resolve the JDK from the project, not a constant** — and use the SAME major for the build and the runtime, because class files from a newer release cannot be loaded by an older JVM. Two traps. (1) The version glob is matched against `java -version` text, so the major must be followed by a dot, whitespace or the closing quote — a bare `21` also matches `210`; there is a test. (2) Zero must mean the default, or every options struct that forgets the field silently changes behaviour. The control worth running: boot a Java **21** project with `JAVA_HOME` pointing at a JDK **25** — it must ignore it and find the 21, and `ps` per-process is the only reliable way to check, since a stale JVM from an earlier run will fool `ps | head -1`. ako/mxcli-maintenance #1 |
